comparisons.peer_summary: Commissions and other fees increased due to higher brokerage commissions and custody fees on higher volume in CIB and AWM, as well as higher annuity sales commissions in CCB.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and JPMorgan (JPM) report increases in commissions and fees driven by higher transaction volumes in their investment and wealth management businesses. GS attributes its 8% increase to higher market volumes in Equities, while JPM cites higher brokerage commissions and custody fees resulting from higher volume in its Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB) and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) segments. Both disclosures highlight volume as a key driver for commission growth, though GS specifically notes a one-time loss from a GM credit card transition offsetting the gains, whereas JPM highlights annuity sales commissions as another contributor.

sentences.text: Commissions and fees in the consolidated statements of earnings were $4.09 billion for 2024, 8% higher than 2023, due to higher commissions and fees in Equities, reflecting generally higher market volumes and increased transaction fees, partially offset by a loss related to the planned transition of the GM credit card program to another issuer.

Commissions and other fees increased, predominantly due to higher brokerage commissions and fees on higher volume, and higher custody fees, in both CIB and AWM, as well as higher annuity sales commissions in CCB.
